Then he said to me, “Be courageous in this service. Tell everyone about the Lord’s mighty works. You will find favor in this service. Anyone who follows these commandments will live and be happy in life. Anyone who ignores them will not live and will be miserable in life.”

2. “Tell everyone who can do what is right to keep doing good works. It benefits them. And I say that everyone should be rescued from hardship. People who are in need and struggle with daily life suffer great torment and distress.”

3. “Anyone who rescues such a person from distress gains great joy. A person suffering this hardship is in as much torment as someone agonizing in chains.[a] Many cannot bear these troubles and bring death on themselves. Anyone who knows about such a person’s trouble but does not rescue them commits a great sin and becomes guilty of that person’s blood.[b]”

4. “All of you who have received from the Lord must do good works. Do not delay until the tower is finished. Work on it has been paused for your sake. Unless you hurry to do what is right, the tower will be finished and you will be shut out.”

5. After speaking with me, he got up from the couch. He took the shepherd and the virgins with him and left. He told me he would send that shepherd and the virgins back to my house.

Restore that relationship and the connective igitur without changing the subsequent exclusion warning, existing notes, or paragraph divisions.

  text: 'Then he said to me, “Conduct yourself courageously in this service. Tell every person about the
    Lord’s mighty works, and you will find favor in this service. Whoever walks in these commandments
    will live and be happy in life. But whoever neglects them will not live and will be miserable in life.”

    hardship suffers the same torment as a person agonizing in chains.[a] Many, unable to bear such calamities,

    commits a great sin and becomes guilty of that person’s blood.[b]”


    4. “Therefore, all of you who have received from the Lord, do good works, lest the tower’s structure
    be completed while you delay doing them. For the work of building it has been suspended for your sake.
    Unless you hurry to do what is right, the tower will be completed and you will be shut out.”


    5. After he had spoken with me, he rose from the couch, took the shepherd and the virgins with him,
    and went away, saying to me that he would send that shepherd and the virgins back to my house.'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The printed Latin literally compares the sufferer with someone who “torments himself” in chains.
      “Agonizing” renders the reflexive anguish; the source has not been silently emended.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The Vulgata base has singular “becomes guilty of that person’s blood” and “commits a great sin.”

      its preceding clause may differ. Much is lost. This draft retains the continuous Latin and does
      not reconstruct the absent Greek sentence.

  alternatives:

  rationale: 'The accusative infinitive is passive: the person is the one rescued, not the grammatical

  chosen: took the shepherd and the virgins with him

  rationale: Preserve departure with the named figures; do not add a new scene or a return that has not
